cross_attention_states.text:
Encoded text (K/V)
The encoded prompt supplies the keys and values here — the latent tokens are the queries, this external text sequence is the K/V, which is what makes it cross-attention. denoiser.text:
U-Net denoiser
The network applied at every step: a 4-stage convolutional U-net (down → mid → up with skip connections) that takes the latent z_t (+ timestep + text conditioning) and predicts the noise. Each down stage halves the spatial resolution (the latent is 8× downscaled at the bottleneck) and each up stage doubles it back; the timestep modulates every ResNet, and text conditioning (dim 768) enters the cross-attention stages. latent.text:
Latent state (z_t)
The working latent — a single slot the loop reads and rewrites each step. It is seeded once from the initial noise (z_T), overwritten every step by the scheduler's output (z_{t-1}), and read by the denoiser as the current z_t. 'z_t' and 'z_{t-1}' are this same slot at consecutive steps, not separate tensors — the two arrows feeding it are two writers at different times, not a sum.
4 channels

noise.text:
Initial noise
z_T: random Gaussian latent, shape [4 channels], sampled in the VAE latent space. (Image-to-image instead starts from an encoded input image.) This is the latent the loop iteratively denoises.

sch_step.text:

scheduler.text:
Scheduler — PNDM
PNDM combines the denoiser's prediction with z_t to produce z_{t-1}, one step toward a clean latent. The loop repeats for N sampling steps (N chosen at inference, typically ~20-50 — it is not a config field).

timestep.text:
Timestep
The current step's noise level t (decreasing T -> 0). Embedded, then projected and added inside every ResNet block (and the mid block) — a U-net conditions on the noise level additively, not through AdaLN.

unet_op_conv1.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

unet_op_conv2.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

unet_op_norm1.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.

unet_op_norm2.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.

unet_op_residual.text:
Residual add
Adds the block's raw input back onto the convolved output — (input_tensor + hidden_states) / output_scale_factor. The bypass goes around the entire cell: norm1, SiLU, conv1, timestep injection, norm2, SiLU, conv2. When in/out channels differ a 1×1 conv adjusts the shortcut (conv_shortcut).

unet_op_temb.text:
⊕ Timestep embedding
The linear-projected timestep embedding is added here (ResnetBlock2D: hidden_states = hidden_states + time_emb_proj(SiLU(temb))). This is the mechanism by which a UNet ResNet receives the current noise level — distinct from DiT/AdaLN, which gates normalization parameters. The projection adjusts the channel width to match the residual branch.

unet_text_cond.text:
Text conditioning
The encoded text prompt supplies the keys/values to EVERY cross-attention stage — the down, mid and up CrossAttn blocks all read the same 768-d text states (in SDXL, the two CLIP encoders' features concatenated). The latent flows through the U vertically; this conditioning enters each cross-attention stage from the side. Click to see how the encoders combine. Declared by cross_attention_dim + the CrossAttn* block types.

vae_op_conv1.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours. The feature-transforming workhorse of the cell; the stack runs GroupNorm + SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

vae_op_conv2.text:
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours. The feature-transforming workhorse of the cell; the stack runs GroupNorm + SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.

vae_op_norm1.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization followed by a SiLU (swish) activation, applied before each convolution in the residual cell. Normalizes feature statistics so the conv sees a well-scaled signal.

vae_op_norm2.text:
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization followed by a SiLU (swish) activation, applied before each convolution in the residual cell. Normalizes feature statistics so the conv sees a well-scaled signal.

vae_op_residual.text:
Residual add
Adds the block input back onto the convolved output (an identity skip, or a 1×1 conv when the channel count changes) so the cell learns a residual and gradients flow cleanly through depth.

vae_op_upsample.text:
Upsample
Doubles spatial resolution (H × W → 2H × 2W) by nearest-neighbour interpolation, then a 3×3 conv to smooth interpolation artifacts. Runs once after the ResNet stack, stepping the latent toward image size.

Latent state (z_t)
The working latent — a single slot the loop reads and rewrites each step. It is seeded once from the initial noise (z_T), overwritten every step by the scheduler's output (z_{t-1}), and read by the denoiser as the current z_t. 'z_t' and 'z_{t-1}' are this same slot at consecutive steps, not separate tensors — the two arrows feeding it are two writers at different times, not a sum.
4 channels
U-Net denoiser
The network applied at every step: a 4-stage convolutional U-net (down → mid → up with skip connections) that takes the latent z_t (+ timestep + text conditioning) and predicts the noise. Each down stage halves the spatial resolution (the latent is 8× downscaled at the bottleneck) and each up stage doubles it back; the timestep modulates every ResNet, and text conditioning (dim 768) enters the cross-attention stages. GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization followed by a SiLU (swish) activation, applied before each convolution in the residual cell. Normalizes feature statistics so the conv sees a well-scaled signal.
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours. The feature-transforming workhorse of the cell; the stack runs GroupNorm + SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization followed by a SiLU (swish) activation, applied before each convolution in the residual cell. Normalizes feature statistics so the conv sees a well-scaled signal.
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours. The feature-transforming workhorse of the cell; the stack runs GroupNorm + SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
Residual add
Adds the block input back onto the convolved output (an identity skip, or a 1×1 conv when the channel count changes) so the cell learns a residual and gradients flow cleanly through depth.
Upsample
Doubles spatial resolution (H × W → 2H × 2W) by nearest-neighbour interpolation, then a 3×3 conv to smooth interpolation artifacts. Runs once after the ResNet stack, stepping the latent toward image size.
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
⊕ Timestep embedding
The linear-projected timestep embedding is added here (ResnetBlock2D: hidden_states = hidden_states + time_emb_proj(SiLU(temb))). This is the mechanism by which a UNet ResNet receives the current noise level — distinct from DiT/AdaLN, which gates normalization parameters. The projection adjusts the channel width to match the residual branch.
GroupNorm + SiLU
Group normalization then a SiLU activation, applied before each convolution so the conv sees a well-scaled signal. GroupNorm is fixed in the ResnetBlock2D class; the activation is resolved through the denoiser's act_fn input.
Conv 3×3
A 3×3 convolution (stride 1, padding 1): mixes each position with its spatial neighbours — the cell runs GroupNorm+SiLU → Conv 3×3 twice.
Residual add
Adds the block's raw input back onto the convolved output — (input_tensor + hidden_states) / output_scale_factor. The bypass goes around the entire cell: norm1, SiLU, conv1, timestep injection, norm2, SiLU, conv2. When in/out channels differ a 1×1 conv adjusts the shortcut (conv_shortcut).
